At the center, the monumental Victorian Gothic Revival St Mary's Cathedral rises with three soaring, sharply delineated sandstone spires—a massive 90m central crossing spire and twin western spires flanking the nave. The streets below, including Palmerston Place and surrounding avenues, are entirely decluttered of vehicles, traffic, dumpsters, and pedestrians, exposing pristine asphalt carriageways, authentic Caithness flagstone footpaths, solid sandstone kerbs, and black wrought-iron lightwell railings. Mature green leafy sycamores and plane trees frame the cathedral grounds with natural organic branching.
